contract.scope: Configuration only, and only for the nine jurisdictions this shard owns. No shared path is touched and no unassigned jurisdiction is touched.
contract.waitingPeriods: No waiting period is authored, shortened, reordered or bound. Every proposal below is evidence for the integration captain: a rule id the jurisdiction's own compiled profile already publishes, that rule's source text quoted verbatim, and the duration exactly as the profile already states it.
contract.activeRecommendations: No fallback-dependent route is recommended ACTIVE. A route still resolving through the provisional prose selector is not release-ready whatever terminal it returns.

CT.detail: Phase 2 reopened Connecticut and it still holds. The bounded sweep over rendered screens reaches packet_ready_with_caution with payment open on petitioned-clean-slate-erasure-for-eligible-pre-2000-convictions-jd-cr-202, matching data/expungement-ai/phase2/remedy-context-replay-after.json. A direct replay returns the same result at all nine timing buckets. Not re-investigated; nothing changed.

NJ.detail: This shard's remaining UX-STATELAW-001 jurisdiction, and the answer is neither of the two the phase offers. New Jersey's blocker is not a missing fact: the bounded sweep reports no unrendered fact the evaluator consumes except record_documents, which Phase 2 recorded as changing no decision in any of the 51. It is not a claim about self-help availability either. A direct replay of the regular-expungement route at every one of the nine timing buckets, including gt_10_years, returns needs_review with reason code nj.waiting_rule_not_executed and missingQuestionIds empty. The timing gate never clears because the waiting rule never resolves, which is exactly the hold Phase 2 recorded. Resolving it means authoring a New Jersey waiting period, which this shard may not do. No lifecycle classification correction is warranted and no escalation of the product claim is warranted; what is warranted is the waiting-rule decision that is already in the counsel queue.

evidence.probe: Regular expungement under N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2 / 2C:52-3, answering only rendered screens, sweeping all nine resolved_timing_bucket values.

NJ.whatThisShardDidNotDo: No lifecycle classification was corrected, because no fact is missing. No product claim was escalated, because the route is not being withdrawn. The waiting-rule decision that already sits in the counsel queue is the whole of it, and authoring it is forbidden here.

Rendering a controlled list means a renderer branch for county (src/components/expungement-ai/**) and a change to the compiled question's type and options, which verify-expungement-plain-language-values locks against origin/main unless data/expungement-ai/screening-parity-approved-deltas.json approves it. All three paths are prohibited to this shard.

step3_issueDispositions.whatWasBuilt: A controlled record-clearing court dataset for all nine, inside each state pack, each qualified by the state's real local unit — judicial district for Connecticut, parish for Louisiana, county elsewhere — and each with a labelled manual-entry fallback.
step3_issueDispositions.whatRemains: The same three prohibited paths as UX-COUNTY-001.

That is a question-model change with a parity approval, both shared.

CT:automatic-non-conviction-erasure-unde.pathwayLabel: Automatic non-conviction erasure under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 54-142a
CT:automatic-non-conviction-erasure-unde.why: wait-02 gives immediate erasure for a dismissal or acquittal and names § 54-142a; wait-03 gives 13 months for a nolle. They are different periods and the fact that would choose between them is not one the participant supplies: CT's case_outcome merges dismissal, no-bill, nolle prosequi and non-prosecution into a single option value, so a participant who answers it cannot be told apart. Choosing either would either delay a dismissal by 13 months or open a nolle 13 months early.

CT:automatic-non-conviction-erasure-unde.unblockedBy: A screening question that separates a nolle from a dismissal. That is a shared question-model change, not a state-pack one.

CT:cannabis-conviction-erasure.why: Connecticut publishes eight waiting-period rules and none of them mentions cannabis. Every candidate the prose selector can reach belongs to the Clean Slate, non-conviction or pardon tables. There is nothing in the repository to bind, and inventing a cannabis erasure period would be authoring legal content.

DE:discretionary-court-expungement-under.pathwayLabel: Discretionary court expungement under 11 Del. C. § 4374
DE:discretionary-court-expungement-under.why: The § 4374 discretionary tier carries four different periods — 3, 5, 7 and 7 years — keyed on whether the misdemeanor is listed in § 4373(b), whether there are multiple cases, and whether a felony is a single nonviolent one. DE's offense_level offers only Misdemeanor, Felony, Infraction or violation and I am not sure, so none of the facts that select between the four is supplied. The candidates conflict and no supplied answer resolves them.

DE:juvenile-expungement-under-10-del-c-1.why: The only route-specific timing the profile publishes for the juvenile route is wait-01, and it describes the Attorney General's 120-day response window and the court's manifest-injustice finding — a post-filing procedural timetable, not a period a participant must wait before filing. Binding it would impose a pre-filing wait the source does not state. The tier table in wait-10 has no juvenile row.

DE:mandatory-and-automatic-expungement-u.pathwayLabel: Mandatory and automatic expungement under 11 Del. C. §§ 4373 and 4373A
DE:mandatory-and-automatic-expungement-u.why: The mandatory tier states None for a case terminated in favour of the accused and for marijuana, paraphernalia and underage-alcohol possession, then 3, 5 and 10 years for violations, a single misdemeanor or § 4756 drug possession, and certain eligible felonies. The None rows are not published as standalone rules with ids, and the conviction rows key on categories DE's case_outcome and offense_level cannot express — in particular which felonies are the "certain eligible felonies". The spread runs from none to ten years, so picking one is authoring.

ID:juvenile-expungement.why: Idaho publishes two waiting-period rules. One is the non-conviction one-year request to Idaho State Police and the other is the Clean Slate five-year rule already bound to ID:clean-slate-shielding-under-idaho-code-67-3004-11. Neither is a juvenile rule, and the juvenile pathway names no waiting-rule text of its own. This is the route the shard prompt flags as having no candidate rule at base, and that is confirmed here.

ID:non-conviction-fingerprint-and-crimin.pathwayLabel: Non-conviction fingerprint and criminal-history expungement under Idaho Code § 67-3004(10)
ID:non-conviction-fingerprint-and-crimin.why: The pathway names exactly two waiting-rule texts and both resolve to published profile rules: wait-01 and wait-02. wait-02 is the Clean Slate five-year rule, which is already bound to the § 67-3004(11) shielding route, so it is not this route's. wait-01 states this route's own precondition in its own terms — not charged within one year, then a written request to Idaho State Police — and carries a structured one-year duration the profile already publishes.

evidence.sourceText: A person arrested or served with a criminal summons who was not charged by indictment or information within one year may submit a written request to Idaho State Police.

IL:adult-conviction-sealing.why: The misdemeanor and municipal-ordinance branch is settled at two years, but the felony branch is not. wait-19 and wait-30 state three years, while wait-37 records that the shortened sealing waiting period — three years to two for certain records — takes effect on 30 June 2026. The evaluator clock is pinned to 1 July 2026, so both statements are live at evaluation time and the profile does not say which records are the "certain records". Two different current periods for the same branch, with no supplied fact choosing between them.

evidence.sourceText: Misdemeanor convictions and municipal ordinance violations 2 years after completing the sentence
Felony convictions not in the 2-year group 3 years after completing the last felony sentence
Misdemeanor conviction / municipal ordinance violation 2 years after completing sentence for sealing
Felony conviction 3 years after completing last felony sentence for sealing
evidence.anchorAsThisProfileStatesIt: completing last felony sentence for sealing

evidence.sourceText: Most provisions take effect June 1 / June 30, 2026; the shortened sealing waiting period (3 to 2 years for certain records) and removal of the drug-test requirement take effect June 30, 2026; and AUTOMATIC sealing does not begin until January 1, 2029, phasing in through 2034. Until automatic sealing is live, the petition-based process remains the only route for most records. The agent must not tell a user their record will be sealed automatically before 2029, and must verify which effective date applies to any given rule.

IL:adult-non-conviction-expungement.why: Illinois publishes one row per non-conviction disposition — acquittal, dismissal, released without charging, and conviction reversed or vacated — and all four state immediate eligibility, so every candidate resolves to the same zero-day period and there is nothing to disambiguate. wait-32 restates the same four rows as a single table and agrees.

IL:cannabis-specific-automatic-or-petiti.why: The only rule that mentions cannabis is wait-13, first-offender probation under listed drug, cannabis, meth and second-chance routes, and it carries no structured duration — its text says only "Seal after waiting period unless excluded". Every other candidate the prose selector reaches belongs to the general supervision, misdemeanor or felony tables. There is no cannabis period in the repository to bind.

evidence.sourceText: First-offender probation under listed drug/cannabis/meth/second-chance routes Seal after waiting period unless excluded

IL:clean-slate-automatic-sealing.why: wait-37 states that automatic sealing does not begin until 1 January 2029 and phases in through 2034, that the petition-based process remains the only route for most records until then, and that the agent must not tell a participant their record will be sealed automatically before 2029. A waiting-period binding for a route that is not yet operating is not meaningful, and the correction needed — what this route claims to a participant before 2029 — changes what the product claims. Under this shard's own instruction that is escalated, not answered.

evidence.sourceText: Automatic sealing will generally cover records already eligible for sealing once the system begins, including non-convictions, completed supervision/probation, most misdemeanors, and most nonviolent felonies, but the person must have completed the sentence, have no pending criminal charges, and satisfy the waiting period. ("https://www.illinoislegalaid.org/legal-information/what-you-need-know-about-clean-slate-act")

Until automatic sealing is live, the petition-based process remains the only route for most records. The agent must not tell a user their record will be sealed automatically before 2029, and must verify which effective date applies to any given rule.

IL:clean-slate-automatic-sealing.escalation: IL Clean Slate automatic sealing is presented as an available remedy context while the profile's own source note says it does not begin until 2029. Owner decision required on what the route should say before then.

IL:criminal-identity-theft-mistaken-iden.why: No Illinois waiting-period rule mentions identity theft or mistaken identity. The rules the pathway names are the trafficking, juvenile, Clean Slate and Wilma-training rows, none of which governs this route. The four immediate non-conviction rows would be the intuitive answer, but the pathway does not name them and reading them across would be authoring, not transcribing.

IL:expungement-after-eligible-supervisio.why: Qualified probation is settled at five years, and source_question_10 is a rendered yes_no_unsure that identifies it. The supervision branch is not: wait-09 gives two years for most successful supervision and wait-10 gives five for supervision on listed Vehicle Code and criminal-code offences, and the profile does not publish the list, so no supplied answer chooses. wait-24 adds a third possibility, age 25. Three different periods, no supplied fact.

IL:felony-prostitution-relief.why: No Illinois waiting-period rule mentions prostitution. wait-21 is the trafficking-survivor rule and is a different route with a different statutory basis. Nothing in the repository states this route's period.

IL:human-trafficking-survivor-vacatur-an.why: wait-21 names this route and no other — vacation and expungement or immediate sealing for a trafficking victim after completing the last sentence — and carries the structured zero-day duration the profile already publishes. It is the only trafficking rule Illinois publishes and it is unconditional within the route.

evidence.sourceText: Illinois allows a trafficking victim to petition for vacation and expungement or immediate sealing after completing the last sentence if participation in the underlying offense resulted from human trafficking or a severe form of trafficking under federal law. The petition must state that the person was a trafficking victim at the time of the offense and that their participation resulted from trafficking; eligibility is shown by a preponderance of the evidence. ("https://www.ilga.gov/documents/legislation/ilcs/documents/002026300K5.2.htm")

KY:felony-conviction-431073.pathwayLabel: Eligible felony conviction vacatur and expungement under KRS 431.073
KY:felony-conviction-431073.why: The pathway names three waiting-rule texts and all three resolve to published profile rules. wait-04 is the only one that states a filing delay, and it states it in this route's own terms. wait-03 is a clean-record condition over the same five years, so it cannot conflict. wait-05 is the post-filing procedural timetable — prosecutor response within 60 days, hearing within 120 — and must not be bound as a waiting period.

evidence.sourceText: The application is filed no sooner than five years after sentence, probation, or parole completion, whichever is later.
evidence.anchorAsThisProfileStatesIt: sentence, probation, or parole completion, whichever is later

openQuestionsForCounsel: wait-05's 60-day figure is a post-filing procedural window. The provisional prose selector can reach it, and if it does it under-states this route's period by nearly five years. That is a reason to bind wait-04 explicitly rather than leave the route on the fallback.

KY:juvenile-automatic-dismissal.pathwayLabel: Juvenile automatic expungement on qualifying dismissal
KY:juvenile-automatic-dismissal.why: The pathway names no waiting-rule text at all, and none of Kentucky's seven published rules mentions a juvenile matter. There is nothing to bind.

KY:juvenile-petition-610330.pathwayLabel: Juvenile petition to vacate and expunge under KRS 610.330
KY:juvenile-petition-610330.why: The pathway names no waiting-rule text, and none of Kentucky's seven published rules mentions KRS 610.330 or a juvenile petition. There is nothing to bind.

KY:misdemeanor-violation-traffic-convict.pathwayLabel: Misdemeanor, violation, or traffic-infraction conviction expungement under KRS 431.078
KY:misdemeanor-violation-traffic-convict.why: The pathway names exactly two waiting-rule texts and both resolve to published profile rules. wait-02 is the filing delay and states it in this route's own terms; wait-01 is a clean-record condition over the same five years and cannot conflict with it.

evidence.sourceText: The petition is filed no sooner than five years after sentence completion or successful completion of probation, whichever is later, except the named voided first-possession routes.
evidence.anchorAsThisProfileStatesIt: sentence completion or successful completion of probation, whichever is later, except the named void

openQuestionsForCounsel: wait-02 carves out "the named voided first-possession routes". The profile does not publish which routes those are, so the carve-out cannot be expressed as a condition. The general five-year rule is proposed; the carve-out stays with counsel.

KY:nonconviction-431076.pathwayLabel: Acquittal, dismissal, or failure-to-indict expungement under KRS 431.076
KY:nonconviction-431076.why: wait-06 gives 60 days for an acquittal or a dismissal with prejudice; wait-07 gives three years for a felony dismissal without prejudice and one year for a misdemeanor one. The fact that chooses — whether the dismissal was with or without prejudice — is not asked, because KY's case_outcome merges dismissal, no-bill, nolle prosequi and non-prosecution into one option. wait-07 also packs two periods into one rule with a single structured duration of three years, so binding it would over-state the misdemeanor branch by two years.

evidence.sourceText: Acquittal or dismissal with prejudice requires at least 60 days before filing and cannot have been exchanged for a guilty plea to another offense.
Felony dismissal without prejudice requires at least three years; misdemeanor dismissal without prejudice requires at least one year.

KY:nonconviction-431076.unblockedBy: A screening question that asks whether the dismissal was with or without prejudice, and a profile that publishes the felony and misdemeanor without-prejudice periods as separate rules. Both are outside this shard.

LA:automated-expungement-status-verifica.why: No Louisiana waiting-period rule mentions Article 985.2 or automated status verification. Every candidate the prose selector reaches belongs to the DWI-diversion, clean-period, marijuana, first-offender-pardon, exclusion or violent-offence rows. There is nothing to bind.

LA:expungement-by-redaction-for-multi-pe.pathwayLabel: Expungement by redaction for multi-person records
LA:expungement-by-redaction-for-multi-pe.why: No Louisiana waiting-period rule mentions redaction or a multi-person record. The seven published rules all belong to other routes.

LA:felony-article-893-e-set-aside-follow.pathwayLabel: Felony Article 893(E) set-aside followed by expungement
LA:felony-article-893-e-set-aside-follow.why: wait-06 mentions Article 893(E) cases, but it does so as one of Article 978's eligibility exceptions, not as a waiting period, and its five-year figure belongs to the CDS sentencing threshold in the same sentence. Reading it as this route's period would be authoring. The clean-period rules wait-02 and wait-04 belong to the five- and ten-year routes, which are separate pathways.

evidence.sourceText: Felony hard exclusions / review flags: Article 978 generally blocks expungement for crimes of violence, sex offenses or offenses against minor victims, many controlled-dangerous-substance offenses outside listed exceptions, and domestic abuse battery. Drug convictions may still be eligible if they fall into Article 978s exceptions, including certain possession offenses, possession with intent to distribute, CDS offenses punishable by not more than five years, Article 893(E) cases, or first-offender-pardon cases. ("https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/Law.aspx?d=919670")

LA:felony-ten-year-clean-period-expungem.why: wait-04 states this route in its own terms — more than ten years since completion of sentence, deferred adjudication, probation or parole, no other conviction in that ten-year period, no pending charge, DA certification required — and carries the structured ten-year duration the profile already publishes. No other Louisiana rule states a ten-year felony clean period for this route; wait-07's ten years belongs to the separate contradictory-hearing exception for named violent offences.

evidence.sourceText: 2 More than ten years have passed since completion of sentence, deferred adjudication, probation, or parole; the person has no other criminal conviction during the ten-year period before filing; and no criminal charge is pending. A DA certification is required.

LA:first-offender-pardon-felony-expungem.why: wait-05 is the only rule that names the first-offender pardon, but it states when the pardon arises — automatically on completion of sentence, once court costs are paid — not when the expungement may be filed. Its structured duration is zero days, so binding it would open a felony packet immediately. That is the direction in which a wrong binding causes harm, and the repository does not say whether a clean period also applies to this route.

evidence.sourceText: Louisianas first-offender pardon statute says a first offender never previously convicted of a felony is automatically pardoned upon completion of sentence without Board of Pardons recommendation or governor action, but no pardon is issued unless court costs for the conviction are paid. ("https://www.legis.la.gov/legis/Law.aspx?d=79202")

evidence.sourceText: New Hampshire has a special marijuana possession annulment statute, RSA 651:5-b. The prosecutor has 10 days to object; if the prosecutor objects, they must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the marijuana amount exceeded 3/4 ounce. reachabilityFromRenderedScreensOnly.note: This shard's remaining UX-STATELAW-001 jurisdiction, and the answer is neither of the two the phase offers. New Jersey's blocker is not a missing fact: the bounded sweep reports no unrendered fact the evaluator consumes except record_documents, which Phase 2 recorded as changing no decision in any of the 51. It is not a claim about self-help availability either. A direct replay of the regular-expungement route at every one of the nine timing buckets, including gt_10_years, returns needs_review with reason code nj.waiting_rule_not_executed and missingQuestionIds empty. The timing gate never clears because the waiting rule never resolves, which is exactly the hold Phase 2 recorded. Resolving it means authoring a New Jersey waiting period, which this shard may not do. No lifecycle classification correction is warranted and no escalation of the product claim is warranted; what is warranted is the waiting-rule decision that is already in the counsel queue.
